title: schema sync: implicit indexes on the system columns created_at (with id) and owner_id — default list order and private-OWD reads (epic #33631 R3/R11)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #33631 (SQL performance; maintainer's direct word on the epic). Items R3 + R11 of the M0 ranked list (#33633): https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889544281, corrected by https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889939163 (review#2 PASS 6890102899).

## Maintainer ruling (seat decision card, 2026-11-15T06:40Z)

「两个都加」: schema sync adds implicit indexes on the two system columns, `created_at` (as `(created_at, id)`, the default list order) and `owner_id` (the column a private-OWD read filters on). This supersedes the earlier implicit-index ruling that excluded system columns for want of a measured read.

## Measured (corrected, 1M rows)

- PostgreSQL: the index alone takes the admin default-ordered page 229 → 0.9 ms (member page 101 → 3.2 ms).
- SQLite: the index does nothing while the vacuous controlled_by_parent chain is in the query; with that chain dropped (the R4 card filed alongside, Blocked-by below) the page goes 1.7 s → 0.09 ms.
- `owner_id`: small at 10k rows (1.6 → 1.4 ms); grows with private-object size.

## Scope

- Seam: schema sync implicit index set (`schema-drift.ts` ~2295) for driver-sql dialects and Turso.
- Before/after on the M0 bench (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf`, PR #33662) in the PR, both dialects.
- SQLite: land with or after the R4 card; PG pays alone.

## Business reason

Every default-ordered list of a large object sorts its whole filtered set today; on PG an admin list of 1M rows answers in ~1 ms instead of ~230 ms.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area A4 (schema sync), next account; size S.

## Dedupe

`is:issue is:open implicit index created_at` → 5 hits, none on this seam (only #33631 and seat posts); `owner_id index system column` → 5, none (#33435 is a lint rule).
